results.label: spoiler-motivation-too-early
results.qa_question: Why is the old fox so grumpy?
results.qa_answer:
Mosk has guarded the secrets of the tree for so long that he has forgotten how to be kind. He fears that if anyone listens to the humming, the magic inside might fade away forever.

The old fox sighed, his whiskers twitching with annoyance as he tapped a polished wooden cane against the floor. He told Lina that the secrets of the roots were heavy, and a little girl’s ears were far too soft to carry the weight of such ancient sounds. But Lina only stepped closer, her red coat bright against the shadows, and asked him what the humming was trying to say.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Even with his heavy secrets and grumpy warnings, Mosk remained still as the shadows stretched long around them. Lina stood her ground, waiting to see if he would let her pass.

replacement_segments.text: Lina stood her ground, her eyes searching his. She knew that behind his gruff words was a deep, hidden fear of losing the magic he protected. Mosk looked at her, his gaze softening just a fraction, realizing that this visitor was not going to leave so easily.

Mosk pointed toward the dark exit, but Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. She set it on the step between them, a quiet peace offering for the trouble of walking her down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time, then he stood up, adjusted his green vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word.

Lina’s heart was far too kind to leave a hungry fox behind, and besides, she knew that generosity often opens doors that force cannot. She watched as Mosk’s whiskers twitched at the scent of the fruit, and she followed him down into the deepening dark. 

The air grew warm and smelled of pine needles and damp earth as they descended. With every step, the humming grew louder, vibrating against the soles of her boots until it felt as though the very ground beneath them was singing a lullaby. Mosk stopped abruptly at a landing lit by a single, glowing mushroom, turning back to see if the little girl in the red coat was still brave enough to follow.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Lina knew that kindness was a stronger key than any trick, and seeing Mosk begin his descent, she stepped into the shadows behind him. The hollow tree hummed a low, welcoming tune as they reached the final, mossy landing.

replacement_segments.text: At the base of the stairs, a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of soft moss, her golden glow flickering like a dying candle. Mosk’s whiskers trembled with a deep, hidden sadness as he looked at her. He whispered that she had been his dearest friend once, but long ago, he had failed to bring her the medicine she needed. Ever since that winter, he had guarded the tree, too ashamed to look her in the eye.

Lina knelt beside the queen, asking gently what could mend her spirit. A drop of warm milk and a kind word was all the queen required, for she knew that was the true secret of all medicine. Mosk hurried to fetch the milk in a tiny thimble, resting his paw beside hers as the queen’s light began to steady. The humming within the tree transformed into a joyous melody, and for the first time in many years, Mosk hummed along.
